shipped_rows.title_o: The long and the short of it: On the nature and origin of functional overlap between representations of space and time
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: "The preregistered stage 1 analytic sample size of N = 144 was met. The group × novelty interaction in the mixed ANOVA was statistically significant, F(1, 142) = 4.47, p = .036, partial η² = .03 (Cohen’s f² = .032). Furthermore, Figure 1 indicates a pattern of means that is consistent with Srinivasan and Carey’s (2010) claim. The congruent group were clearly able to distinguish between the familiar (M = 4.14, SD = 0.60) and novel (M = 2.92, SD = 0.95) pairings, t(67) = 9.61, p < .001, dz = 1.17. The incongruent group were also clearly able to distinguish between the familiar (M = 3.90, SD = 0.60) and novel (M = 3.05, SD = 0.95) pairings, though somewhat less well, t(75) = 7.10, p < .001, dz = 0.81. We therefore conclude that the SCORE H* claim has been replicated, although it should be noted our interaction effect was only around 1/4th of the size of that observed by the original authors."

prior_scientific_decisions.quote: In the results quoted above, Srinivasan and Carey (2010) reported p-values for 11 effects. We replicated all seven that were p < .05. We observed p < .05 for the four effects that Srinivasan and Carey (2010) reported as non-significant. However the size and direction of our effects were consistent with the trends reported in the original paper. It is therefore likely that statistical power may account for at least some of the differences observed between the original and replication studies.
prior_scientific_decisions.reason: Although the authors conclude that the focal SCORE H* group-by-novelty interaction claim was replicated, their preregistered replication of the eleven effects in Section 4.2 of Srinivasan and Carey (2010) explicitly contrasts four effects where the incongruent group significantly detected novelty despite non-significant results in the original study. Because confirming the focal effect is not an overall verdict on all tested findings and the authors explicitly identify these four discrepancies alongside the seven replicated effects, the paper-level outcome is mixed.
